name: solo-0023-voice-timeline-renderer
summary: HTTP service for validated PCM WAV ingestion, assembly timelines, and normalized mixdowns.

modules.responsibility: Public HTTP routes, identity headers, request limits, JSON errors, and media responses.
Single permission authority for project membership, roles, grant resolution, and the render publication gate.
Workflow orchestration, permission-aware resource resolution, grants, legacy adoption, and render lifecycle.
Entities, project ownership, grants, validation rules, stable errors, and state transitions.
PCM WAV decoding and encoding, resampling, channel mapping, and metrics.
Timeline evaluation, crossfade mixing, normalization, and authorization-aware receipts.
Concurrent-safe atomic persistence for projects, grants, media, metadata, and legacy adoption.

workflows.name: Register audio source
steps: Apply request size and identity validation
Decode PCM WAV and measure the signal
Atomically persist media and metadata
workflows.success: Returns immutable source metadata that can be read back.
workflows.failure: Returns a stable validation error and leaves no visible source.
workflows.verification: The workflow check registers a generated WAV, reads it back, and rejects a malformed payload.

workflows.name: Compose assembly timeline
steps: Validate span count, ranges, gain, and crossfade constraints
Resolve source references from storage
Persist a ready timeline only after all spans pass
workflows.success: Returns a ready timeline with stable source references.
workflows.failure: Returns the first stable timeline validation error without partial persistence.
workflows.verification: The workflow check composes a valid two-span timeline and rejects an impossible crossfade.

workflows.name: Render timeline mixdown
steps: Create and advance a durable render job
Resample, map channels, apply gains and fades, then crossfade spans
Normalize, atomically commit output and receipt, and complete the job
workflows.success: Returns a completed job whose WAV and receipt match.
workflows.failure: Returns a terminal failed job with a stable error code and no partial output.
workflows.verification: The workflow check renders a crossfaded timeline, decodes the result, and compares receipt measurements.

workflows.name: Enforce project isolation and roles
steps: Resolve membership and role through the authorization guard
Deny cross-project reads and references with not-found responses
Block viewer writes while allowing viewer reads
workflows.success: Only project members access project objects; roles limit writes.
workflows.failure: Cross-project object existence leaks or a role boundary is bypassed.
workflows.verification: The workflow check asserts not-found equivalence, non-member rejection, and viewer write denial.

workflows.name: Grant read-only cross-project source use
workflows.entry: PUT /v1/grants then grantee timeline and render routes
steps: Owner issues a read-only grant over an owned source
Grantee reads the source and renders it in its own project
Receipt records the grant authorization basis without a mutation path
workflows.success: The grantee consumes the source legally while source facts stay owner-controlled.
workflows.failure: The grantee can mutate the source, or a third project gains access.
workflows.verification: The workflow check renders through the grant and asserts the receipt basis and third-party isolation.

workflows.name: Revoke grants against in-progress renders
steps: Re-verify every authorization basis immediately before publishing
Fail renders whose grant was withdrawn and publish no artifact
Keep completed receipts explaining the basis legal at their time
workflows.success: No post-revocation artifact is published; historical artifacts stay explainable.
workflows.failure: A render commits after its grant was revoked, or historical receipts lose their basis.
workflows.verification: The workflow check uses a deterministic pre-finalize hook plus post-revocation requests.

workflows.name: Adopt pre-isolation data into a project
steps: Enumerate records lacking project ownership
Stamp one project's ownership and write an adoption manifest
Backfill historical receipts and leave owned records untouched
workflows.success: Adopted records are usable by their new project; unadopted records stay invisible.
workflows.failure: Legacy data is reachable through a separate permission path or owned data is reassigned.
workflows.verification: The workflow check stages unowned records, adopts them, and verifies rendering and second-adoption no-op.
